summary: Recorded the compaction question's state precisely rather than starting a probe I could not finish in the remaining budget: the path-absence side is settled by inspection (handle methods, Command variants and the actor's calls into the core were all checked, so no compaction reaches the instance the actor consumed), and the discriminator now names exactly what would still change the judgment — (i) executing the failure side, a Storage implementation whose write returns Err driven through the actor, to see whether the core's fatal write error really ends the actor task and whether every caller-visible endpoint then collapses to AppendError::Shutdown / RuntimeProposeErr::Shutdown as the source chain implies, or whether the layer surfaces something distinguishable (which would narrow the attribution part), and (ii) any documentation stating compaction is deliberately out of scope for the layer (which would limit the first part to a capability gap). I checked the snapshot's atomic-storage test file for a reusable failing-storage wrapper before deciding; it does not provide one in a directly reusable form, so that probe remains the declared next action rather than a rushed guess. Final position of the audit, unchanged by this turn: four findings — the actor layer's event egress parks the loop and stalls the cluster at capacities 8/64/1024 under a corrected transport (receipts ff4511e8, 76557a28, bbff5b4c, with a 21.69s retrospective bound and the superseded transport-jam run kept as an excluded cause); the core has no timer-driven repair for a lost Accepted, now measured at two and three nodes with quorum-critical losses (receipts 092538c6, 9f3f25cc, one open accounting question closed by explanation); append_notify can resolve Ok for an index occupied by another entry, bounded by measurement to unadopted entries (receipts 743518e2, 78c53df3); and the actor layer owns the instance but offers no compaction path, with the panic-to-Shutdown attribution chain and the repository's own compaction documentation as the norm (source-settled, failure side not yet exercised).
